$doc: The core memory: where the front's ranges begin, and how much a device is
asked to reserve. The page they are counted in is the guest's (xpute-guest
mem/section.rs PAGE_BYTES).
Every one of these is read by more than one language or by more than one
stage of the build, which is why they are here rather than in any of them:
rust/client/kernel/src/sys/mem/section.rs    the map — the fixed ranges and the heap
rust/client/kernel/src/door/layout.rs        the front — the rings and the directory
rust/client-bracket/wasm/build.rs            the linker flags for the module
ts/client/src/abi/boot.ts                    the reservation a tab makes, handed to the page
rust/client-bracket/native/src/lib.rs        the memory a device is given
The stack, at the bottom of the memory. build.rs hands this number to wasm-ld
as `-z stack-size` with `--stack-first`, and the kernel asserts at boot that
the linker's `__stack_high` is where it says, so the ranges above are placed
against the stack the module was actually linked with rather than against a
default that happens to agree.
First so that an overflow goes below zero, wraps as an unsigned 32-bit
address and lands outside the memory, which traps. With the stack after the
data it would write over `.data` silently instead. There is no MMU here and
so no guard page: the wraparound is the whole of the protection.
The kernel's thread's stack on a device, where the kernel is a library on a thread
of its own (rust/client-bracket/native): a main thread's 8 MiB, since React
Native's JavaScript thread has 1 MiB and wgpu's depth has no bound to state.
Frames the submission ring holds, and so payloads: one a slot. A power of
two, which the ring checks, since a position is taken modulo it by masking.
Sized to what a turn is sent, not to a burst: a full ring loses nothing, since
the shell rings with no quota until there is room (@xpute/host/ipc/doorbell.ts
`writer`, `submit`). And small because every slot ends up resident: a
position only grows, so each slot is written in turn, and a slot is a page
since a WORLD_SOURCE's or a CHAT_SEND's packet can come near one.
Frames the completion ring holds: everything one turn leaves, since the
shell reads it dry before it rings again. A turn leaves at most a reply to
each command it applies and its own events after the drain (door.rs
`EVENTS`), so a ring of the submission ring's capacity plus the door's
reserve, `EVENTS` + 1, never stops a drain partway; twice is the present
sizing, a power of two past that. Nothing is overrun if it is short: a
command whose events and reply would not fit waits for the next turn
(xpute-guest ipc/door.rs). A power of two, as the submission ring's.
Where the rings' descriptors begin: the first page past the stack.
Where the rings' payloads begin. Past the descriptors with room to spare, so
that a ring deepened does not move the payloads of the ring before it.
Where the kernel's directory is (xpute-guest ipc/directory.rs): the page under
GLOBAL_BASE, past the rings' payloads. At an address both sides are built with
rather than one the module hands out, so the shell finds it with no call but the
first turn's, which lays the memory out and writes it.
Where the linker may start placing `.rodata`, `.data` and `.bss` — passed to
wasm-ld as `--global-base`, which is the only way to keep it out of the range
the rings take.
A round number rather than wherever the rings happen to end, so the two
ranges grow without moving each other: the rings have everything below it and
the module's own data everything above.
The heap a phone is guaranteed, and so what everything in front of it is
checked against: the stack, the rings, the module's data and the fixed
ranges together must leave this much of PHONE_BYTES.
Measured from where `.heap` begins, because that is the quantity that
matters — where the module's data happens to end is only interesting for
pushing that figure up. Which lets one number stand for the whole front,
and lets the question be asked twice: at compile time against the lowest
the heap could possibly start (`--global-base` plus the fixed ranges, both
constants), so a terrain grown past a phone fails to build; and at boot
against where it actually started and what the device actually gave.
256 MiB. The fixed ranges take 79.04 MiB, the terrain's 65.65 MiB of
them, and the module's data ends at about 10.5 MiB (`__data_end` in a
build), which leaves the phone 422.4 in practice, so there are 166 MiB of
headroom over the guarantee (2026-10-24).
The heap's bounded flows at their worst are checked against it at compile
time too (door/layout.rs `HEAP_FLOWS_BYTES`): the runs that `BODY_SLOTS`
terrain and Earth bodies fill (sys/io/body.rs), a body on every credit in
the buddy's block for a division's, the ways' pool's mirror at its cap
and every read's room for a brick's records at its most, and the
profiler's lanes while its setting is on, each in the buddy's blocks,
a power of two, 204.58 MiB.
Each figure here in MiB to two places is held to the code by a test
(door/layout.test.rs); the data's end is a build's, and read off one.
What a device's memory is counted in: a reservation is a whole number of
these and the bytes past the last one are left out.
What a handheld is asked to reserve. Half of the desktop's, because a
reservation is committed lazily by the OS but JavaScriptCore reports the
whole of it as the page's JavaScript memory — a Safari heap timeline read it
as one ArrayBuffer.
Also the floor the module declares to the engine (`--initial-memory`), so a
shell that asks for less fails to instantiate rather than booting into a
kernel with nowhere to put the terrain.
What everything else is asked to reserve.
